propositions: A longitudinal read-only audit of 2,265 current work tickets and 2,349 reachable commits over 68 days (2026-06-08 through 2026-08-15) reveals planning, throughput, code-review, defect-measurement, and debt signals, with process-maturation confounders and metadata gaps explicitly identified.

Plan-review first-pass rate is 49.0% with p90 attempts = 8, consuming 116,560 LLM calls; review-before-claim adoption rose from 29.2% to 79.5% (Q2→Q3), but deterministic preflight criteria and completion reason classification are absent.

Completion first-pass rate is 72.3%; tickets with Testing headings or file-impact declarations show 79.7%/74.2% first-pass versus 68.6%/67.6% undeclared, but causal claims are unsupported by the evidence.

No current bug record includes detected_by metadata (1.1% coverage across 648 bugs), preventing true escaped-defect rate or detection-stage efficiency measurement; caused_by links are advisory, demonstrably noisy, and auto-generated by blame attribution.

Commit process governance (ticket trailer, DCO, Change-Id) reached ~100% adoption by August; source diffs became smaller (median 111.5→95 lines) and test co-change increased (median 84.5→160.5 lines) from Q2→Q3, supporting process maturation.

Thirty-five modules are at or above 720 LOC (15 above 780 LOC, 4 at 800 LOC); duplication is 4.09%; same-file retouch within 24h covers 47.7% of consecutive pairs—these are debt pressure and hotspot signals requiring tiered, risk-based remediation.
